title: Simplex transport in the explicit cone-weight unstraightening
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes containing all displayed constructions. Use the coherent realization/nerve adjunction and $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and the cone-weight unstraightening $U_K$ and its natural fibre comparisons of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Let $K$ be a small quasicategory, $A=\mathfrak C[K]^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $F:A\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ an enriched functor. Let $m_F:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ be its transpose under $\mathfrak C[K^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong A$. Under the natural equivalences $(U_KF)_k\simeq F(k)$, transport obtained by lifting in the right fibration $U_KF\to K$ agrees coherently with the action of $F$. For an edge $a:k\to l$ it is identified with $F(a):F(l)\to F(k)$. More precisely, a simplex of $U_KF$ over $\sigma:\Delta^r\to K$, represented by an enriched map $T_\sigma\to F$, restricts at the vertices to the fibre values; its subset-poset generators give the homotopies identifying a source value with the action on a target value, and union of subsets gives their iterated composition coherences. These comparisons commute with all faces, degeneracies, enriched maps $F\to G$, and additional simplicial parameters. A homotopy equivalence $E\to U_KF$ over $K$ identifies these same comparisons with the simplex lifts in $E$, using the induced fibre equivalences.

proof.text: Fix a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^r\to K$. The explicit cone presentation of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] says that an $r$-simplex of $U_KF$ over $\sigma$ is an enriched natural map $T_\sigma\to F$, equivalently a simplicial functor from the ordered cone $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r\star\Delta^0]$ to the collage obtained by adjoining a terminal cone vertex with mixed mapping object $F$. Restriction to the initial vertices gives the values $F(\sigma(i))$. The fiber comparison and simplexwise formula of [lem-coef-unstraightening-simplex-pointwise] identify these restrictions with the stated natural equivalences $(U_KF)_k\simeq F(k)$, functorially in $F$ and in the base simplex.

source.place: HTT §2.2.1, Proposition 2.2.1.1 and the cone formula; the explicit fiber calculation of §2.2.2

proof.text: In the subset-poset model of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], the mapping simplicial set from $i$ to $j$ in $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r]$ (and in the cone $\mathfrak C[\Delta^r\star\Delta^0]=\mathfrak C[\Delta^{r+1}]$, with cone vertex $v=r+1$) is the nerve of the inclusion poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing both endpoints, and composition is union. For the cone functor $\Phi$ of Step 1, a subset $I\ni i,v$ is sent to a vertex $\Phi(I)$ of $F(\sigma(i))$, and a flag $I_0\subset\cdots\subset I_q$ of such subsets to a $q$-simplex of $F(\sigma(i))$. The vertex value at $i$ is $\Phi(\{i,v\})$. Since a subset $I\ni i,v$ with second element $j$ is the union $I=(I\setminus\{i\})\cup\{i,j\}$, functoriality of $\Phi$ and the mixed composition of the collage give $\Phi(I)=F(\Phi\{i,j\})\bigl(\Phi(I\setminus\{i\})\bigr)$, where $\Phi\{i,j\}$ is the image of $\{i,j\}$ in $\mathfrak C[K](\sigma(i),\sigma(j))=A(\sigma(j),\sigma(i))$; more generally the restriction of $\Phi$ to flags is the enriched action of $F$ on the image in $\mathfrak C[K]$ of the corresponding flags of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$. Thus these equations are exactly the enriched functor equations for $F$, the opposite on $A$ accounting for the contravariant direction.

source.place: HTT §§1.1.5 and 2.2.1–2.2.3, explicit subset-poset and collage calculation

proof.text: For an edge $a:k\to l$ of $K$, apply Steps 1 and 2 to the one-simplex $\sigma=a$; the cone vertex is $v=2$. The generator $\{0,1\}$ goes to the vertex $a$ of $\mathfrak C[K](k,l)=A(l,k)$; put $x_l=\Phi(\{1,2\})\in F(l)_0$ and $x_k=\Phi(\{0,2\})\in F(k)_0$, the values of the simplex at its two vertices. Since $\{0,1,2\}=\{1,2\}\cup\{0,1\}$, the mixed composition equation gives $\Phi(\{0,1,2\})=F(a)(x_l)$, where $F(a):F(l)\to F(k)$ is the action of $a$ regarded as an arrow $l\to k$ of $A$. The only nondegenerate edge of the mapping set from $0$ to $2$, namely $\{0,2\}\subset\{0,1,2\}$, therefore gives an edge of the Kan complex $F(k)$ from $x_k$ to $F(a)(x_l)$. Conversely $x_k=F(a)(x_l)$ with the degenerate edge defines such a simplex. Since $Q^0=\Delta^0$ in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], the vertices of the fibres $(U_KF)_k\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q F(k)$ are the vertices of $F(k)$, and the comparison $F(k)\to\operatorname{Sing}_QF(k)$ is the identity on vertices. Hence every lift of $a$ with target $x_l$ has source joined to $F(a)(x_l)$ by the displayed edge, and $F(a)(x_l)$ itself is the source of a lift: the lifted transport is $F(a)$ up to these specified homotopies. The same computation after product with $\Delta^q$ (the enriched mapping complexes of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]), with $x_l$ replaced by a $q$-parameter family, gives the statement for the transport map of Kan complexes. The transpose $m_F:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ is defined from these same enriched maps under $\mathfrak C[K^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong A$, so its edge $l\to k$ of $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the vertex $F(a)$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(F(l),F(k))$.

source.place: HTT §2.2.1, simplex collage formula; space-valued straightening transport clause

proof.text: For a general $r$-simplex, a flag of nested endpoint-containing subsets is precisely a simplex of the subset-poset nerve in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Faces and degeneracies restrict or repeat the flag, while the composite of two generators is represented by the union of their subsets. The union law is associative and unital, so the resulting homotopies identify each source value with the action on each target value and identify every iterated composite with the corresponding composite of $F$. The same restriction maps are the simplex operators in the cone formula of Step 1, so these homotopies commute with all faces and degeneracies and give the asserted coherent composition data.

source.place: HTT §§1.1.5 and 2.2.3, subset-poset union composition and coherent nerve

proof.text: All constructions in Steps 1–4 are by restriction of cone functors, postcomposition with an enriched map $F\to G$, and products with a simplicial parameter. The operator maps in the cone presentation are induced by restriction along the corresponding monotone map, and the enriched mapping complexes in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] are maps over $K$ after products with $\Delta^q$. Consequently the edge comparison, every subset-generator homotopy, and every union-composition homotopy commute with faces, degeneracies, enriched maps, and additional simplicial parameters. This is exactly the asserted naturality.

source.place: HTT §2.2.3, naturality of the cone construction and enriched mapping complexes

proof.text: Finally let $h:E\to U_KF$ be a homotopy equivalence over $K$, that is, a map over $K$ with an inverse $g$ and homotopies $E\times\Delta^1\to E$, $U_KF\times\Delta^1\to U_KF$ over $K$, as in the right-fibration category $\mathsf{RFib}(K)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Since $F$ is objectwise Kan it is projectively fibrant; $U_K$ is right Quillen for a model structure whose fibrant objects are the right fibrations, so $U_KF\to K$ is a right fibration, and its vertex fibres are Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] (also by $\operatorname{Sing}_QF(k)$ in [lem-coef-unstraightening-simplex-pointwise]); the same node gives Kan fibres of $E$ when $E\to K$ is a right fibration. Because $h$, $g$ and the homotopies lie over $K$, they restrict to the strict fibres over each vertex $k$ (a homotopy over $K$ maps $E_k\times\Delta^1$ into $E_k$), giving the induced fibre homotopy equivalences $h_k:E_k\to(U_KF)_k$. Applying $h$ to a simplex lift in $E$ over $\sigma$ gives a simplex of $U_KF$ over the same $\sigma$, commuting with faces and degeneracies; its vertex values are the images under $h_k$, and Steps 2--4 compute its generator and composition homotopies. Applying $g$ and the two fibre homotopies in the same way identifies the subset-generator and union-composition comparisons for lifts in $E$ with those in $U_KF$, up to the induced fibre equivalences. This proves the final clause.
